v6_0_2.fix_0: [Library] Uninstalling an Epic game removed the Epic launcher instead: Windows gives it the folder that holds every game, and Cassini read that as the game itself. Ubisoft Connect and HoYoPlay set the same trap. A launcher can no longer answer for one of its games, and the message now points to the one that installed it
v6_0_2.fix_1: [Library] The uninstall confirmation names the program that will really open when it does not carry the game's name: that is what was missing to catch the mistake before making it
v6_0_2.fix_2: [Updates] The update check used to send an authorization token that no longer served any purpose, and that shipped in plain text inside the installed app. It has been removed and revoked. Worth knowing: 6.0.1 and earlier no longer see any update, and say nothing about it. Reinstall once by hand from GitHub; your library and settings are kept
v6_0_2.fix_3: [Solar system] The launcher rail buttons announced themselves as "S" or "E" to a screen reader instead of "Steam, 3 games". They now carry their full name
v6_0_2.change_0: [Updates] Updates now come from the Cassini repository itself, which is public. The separate repo that served them existed only because this one was private

v6_0_1.new_0: [Music] A fourth ambient track, fourteen minutes long: the rotation now has four, and repeats far less
v6_0_1.change_0: [Music] Ambience and event music go quiet while the window is not in front, and pick up again on return. The player keeps going: a track you put on yourself has no business stopping because you opened another window — and the tray menu pauses it without reopening the app
v6_0_1.change_1: [Solar system] The trip from one system to another takes a little longer: three to six seconds depending on distance, instead of two and a half to four and a half
v6_0_1.fix_0: [Solar system] Keyboard speed finally matches the system you are in: it stayed locked to the one at startup, so you crawled through a large system after travelling to it

v6_0_0.new_0: [Solar system] Fully recomputed sky: the Milky Way is a real concentration of stars, with its dust lanes and emission nebulae. It stays sharp at any zoom, and new stars appear as you get closer
v6_0_0.new_1: [Solar system] The sky comes alive: drifting curtains of ionised gas, occasional magnetic storms, shooting stars, and rare travellers crossing in a straight line
v6_0_0.new_2: [Solar system] A sky event can be seen from any corner of the galaxy: it does not fade with distance, and stays in the patch of sky where it happens
v6_0_0.new_3: [Solar system] Comets cross the systems, and their tail is pushed away from the sun whatever they do — one moving away therefore pushes it ahead of itself
v6_0_0.new_4: [Solar system] One more rare event: a vast blue comet sailing over the galaxy — hover it to hear it
v6_0_0.new_5: [Solar system] The supernova now explodes instead of lighting up: a flash, then a torn shell that opens over the whole minute, cools from blue to copper and finally disperses — as large as the black hole
v6_0_0.new_6: [Solar system] A giant black hole appears in the sky: its shadow, its photon ring and its disc bent over the top — the rarest event of all, once a session at most
v6_0_0.new_7: [Achievements] Seven achievements to earn, one per sky event: they unlock if you actually watched the thing go by, not merely if it happened — with a notification, a little chime, and a settings tab showing which ones are missing
v6_0_0.new_8: [Graphics] Sky events can be turned off separately from the gas curtain, and each of the three big ones — supernova, blue comet, black hole — can carry its own music: yours, or one drawn at random from the folder
v6_0_0.new_9: [Settings] Music volume can be set event by event, like the ambient one
v6_0_0.new_10: [Graphics] A tab of its own in the settings, laid out like a game's graphics menu: Low / Medium / High / Ultra preset, render scale from 50 to 200%, frame rate limit, frame counter, star density and bloom
v6_0_0.new_11: [Graphics] “Living sky” can be switched off, for modest machines
v6_0_0.new_12: [Controls] Free-flight speed is now adjustable, from 0.25× to 5×, and starts out brisker
v6_0_0.new_13: [Library] A banner warns when there is no network, and says that missing cover art will load once it is back
v6_0_0.new_14: [Solar system] Events happen anywhere in the sky rather than in front of the camera: you have to be looking the right way, and you can miss them entirely
v6_0_0.change_0: [Music] Nothing plays while the window is not in front: ambience, player and event music all stop as soon as another application covers it, and pick up again on return
v6_0_0.change_1: [Settings] Settings now speak the instrument panel's language: engraved buttons, graduated faders, colour plates, ruled titles — and the tabs wrap instead of overflowing
v6_0_0.change_2: [Interface] Everything moves on a spring: cards and lists arrive in a cascade, dialogs rise out of a blur, and every button answers to hover and press
v6_0_0.change_3: [Solar system] The trip from one system to another has been redone: the camera now looks where it is going instead of staring at the ground halfway, it arrives at a three-quarter angle rather than from above, and starts and stops without a jolt
v6_0_0.fix_0: [Release notes] “Don’t show again” now sticks: the choice was lost at every update
v6_0_0.fix_1: [Library] Cover art comes back on its own once the network returns: an outage used to mark it as non-existent for the whole session, and refreshing changed nothing. The outage is now detected natively, since the web engine does not report it inside the app
v6_0_0.fix_2: [Solar system] Systems stay visible from anywhere: seen from very far away only a star remains — one that shrinks with distance without ever vanishing, and without the launcher name
v6_0_0.perf_0: [Performance] The dedicated graphics card is now claimed at the right moment: on a dual-GPU laptop the scene ran on the integrated chip. Five to six times faster, measured
v6_0_0.perf_1: [Performance] The sky needs no texture at all: 8 MB of graphics memory and a second of startup drawing saved

trainee.detail: It was only a grain of sand. It burned up 80 km above your head, after drifting around the solar system for longer than the Earth has existed.

tempete.detail: The sun's wind slams into the magnetic field, and that is what lights up the sky. In 1859, a storm of that kind set telegraph paper on fire.

comete.detail: The sun's wind blows against the comet and pushes its tail away from the star. That is why a comet moving away from the sun travels tail first.

vaisseau.detail: Something crossed the sky in a straight line, then vanished. In 2017, an object from another star made the same trip through the solar system, and nobody ever managed to say what it was.

cometeBleue.detail: That blue does not come from ice: it is carbon monoxide, ionised by the sun, that starts to glow. It will be back in a few thousand years.

supernova.detail: For a few days, that star shone brighter than the hundred billion stars of its galaxy put together. The last one seen with the naked eye in ours was in 1604.

trouNoir.detail: Its mass bends the light going past and swallows anything that comes too close. That is why its shadow is two and a half times wider than it is.

reseau.horsLigneDetail: Missing cover art will load once the network is back.
